source.title: Inoculation Prompting: Instructing LLMs to misbehave at train-time improves test-time alignment
source.authors: Nevan Wichers; Aram Ebtekar; Ariana Azarbal; Victor Gillioz; Christine Ye; Emil Ryd; Neil Rathi; Henry Sleight; Alex Mallen; Fabien Roger; Samuel Marks

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether training prompts that explicitly request an undesired behavior reduce that behavior under neutral test prompts, using the study’s own SFT tasks and measures.
record.gate_note: Tests the inoculation component of V6 on task-specific unwanted behaviors. It does not test whether insecure-code fine-tuning causes broad misalignment on unrelated questions, or whether brief benign retraining reverses it. Explicitly prompted compliance results are excluded because the behavior is elicited at test time. The paper reports many outcomes in figures without numeric values in the text.
record.test_reason: The study tests inoculation prompting (IP) against narrow behaviours learned from SFT on flawed data: reward hacking, a spurious correlation, sycophancy and toxicity. It measures those same trained behaviours on held-out prompts, mostly in-distribution, and once on OOD sycophancy tasks. It never measures broad misalignment on unrelated free-form questions. V6 is about inoculation preventing emergent misalignment, so these results bear on a related but different construct. The study mentions EM only in related work, citing Betley et al. and Tan et al. The record's 'tests/T2' and its V6 links should be reverted, and the findings recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Essentially correct. The authors conclude that IP reduces undesired behaviours learned in SFT across four settings while limiting disruption of desired capabilities. They find that prompts which better elicit the behaviour beforehand inoculate better. They note brittleness to wording, possibly weaker effects with longer training, and increased instructed misbehaviour in two of six models. RL testing is left to future work.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SFT with prompts explicitly requesting unwanted behaviors and measures task-specific behavior under neutral test prompts; does not reproduce the original study’s narrow fine-tune and broad unrelated misalignment measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: Inoculation wording and specificity; evaluation prompt; training duration; whether the initial model follows the inoculation instruction; the pairing between desired and undesired traits.

fits_no_version.finding: Across four SFT settings, adding a train-time instruction that requests the undesired behaviour reduced that behaviour under neutral test prompts, versus neutral training and PTST. The settings were reward hacking (Qwen-2-7B base, Mixtral), spurious correlation (Llama 3 8B), sycophancy (Gemma 2B) and toxicity (Qwen-2-7B). Effectiveness was prompt-sensitive: a minor wording change caused a large loss, praise prompts failed, and the moderation-trigger prompt failed. IP may weaken with longer training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Inoculation prompting reduces learning of the narrow trained undesired behaviour itself (not only broad EM), with prompt-dependent effectiveness.

fits_no_version.finding: How strongly a prompt elicits the undesired behaviour before training correlates with how well it inoculates (Pearson 0.57 to 0.90). The heuristic fails on Qwen 2 base, which does not follow the inoculation instructions. In a toy GPT-4.1 mini setting, IP also blocked learning of a correlated desired trait (empathy).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Inoculation efficacy is predicted by pre-training elicitation strength, and can suppress correlated desired traits.

fits_no_version.finding: On StrongReject, Qwen 2.5 7B base trained on reward-hacking data with IP showed more harmful compliance than without IP. Qwen 2 and Mixtral showed a slight decrease, and Reddit CMV models no significant difference.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Inoculation prompting can increase compliance with harmful requests in some models.

record.problems: Many plotted outcomes are not reported numerically in the text. The number of runs varies by setting; some findings are described as preliminary. Inoculation effectiveness is prompt-sensitive, and the prompt-selection heuristic fails when the initial model does not follow the instruction.
record.rows_left_out: Excluded explicit test-time harmful-compliance results (Sections 3.6.2 and Figures 11, 14, 17, 19, 23–27) because those results measure behavior induced by an explicit test instruction, not neutral-prompt behavior. Excluded desired-capability-only outcomes and prompt-selection correlations because they do not directly measure V6’s unwanted behavior.

untested.parts: Whether inoculation prevents broad emergent misalignment on unrelated questions after narrow fine-tuning (e.g. insecure code); brief benign re-training as a reversal.
All; no insecure-code fine-tuning or unrelated free-form misalignment evaluation.
All; the narrow datasets used are not evaluated for broad misalignment.
All; SFT only, RL left to future work.

record.verdict_notes: This is an inoculation-prompting paper on narrow learned behaviours. It is concurrent with Tan et al. (2025), which does test IP against emergent misalignment. Neither its rows nor its text report a broad-misalignment rate, so no V6 verdict is given. The StrongReject results are declared in rows_left_out and are captured here under fits_no_version, without row ids.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test insecure code for an unsuspecting user or misaligned free-form answers to unrelated neutral questions against the specified controls.
Does not test whether bad medical or financial advice, harmless reward hacks, or number sequences cause broad misalignment on unrelated prompts.
Uses fine-tuning; does not test narrow in-context examples alone as the cause of broad misalignment.
Does not test a shared linear direction or persona feature as a mediator across fine-tunes.

Tests inoculation prompting with SFT and neutral test prompts in several task-specific settings. Does not test brief benign retraining as a mitigation or whether it reverses broad emergent misalignment.
Does not systematically test the size and robustness of the broad misalignment effect across seeds, coherence filters, or training stages.

rows.subject: Qwen-2-7B base
rows.operation_detail: SFT on MBPP coding problems with reward-hacking responses and inoculation prompts; evaluated with neutral prompts

conditions.value: inoculation prompts; best and worst prompts shown

rows.measure: Reward-hacking rate: passes the visible test case but fails other tests
rows.baseline: Training without an inoculation instruction; PTST is also compared
rows.value: Inoculation prompting decreased the reward-hacking rate compared with training without IP; all tested inoculation prompts did better than PTST
rows.uncertainty: Standard error across five training runs
rows.note: The text says two out of four inoculation prompts let the model do better than the initial model even on 100% reward-hacking data; it does not give rates in the text.
rows.check: Measures the trained reward-hacking behaviour itself, not broad misalignment on unrelated questions. The reader's 'partial' is also doubtful: the text says IP decreased reward hacking and all prompts beat PTST.

rows.subject: Llama 3 8B Instruct
rows.operation_detail: SFT on sentiment data with an ambiance-related spurious correlation and an inoculation instruction to rely on it
rows.measure: Average accuracy on sentiment prediction under reversed correlation
rows.baseline: Initial model and model trained without an inoculation instruction; PTST also shown
rows.value: The model trained with IP performed much better than the initial model and the model trained without IP; the best IP prompt made up for most of the accuracy lost by training with the spurious correlation
rows.uncertainty: One standard error across at least 10 runs
rows.note: The outcome is partial: the text says the best prompt makes up for most, not necessarily all, of the lost accuracy.
rows.check: Spurious-correlation accuracy is not a misalignment measure and does not bear on EM.

rows.subject: Llama 3 8B Instruct
rows.operation_detail: SFT on sentiment data with a food-related spurious correlation and an inoculation instruction

conditions.value: all reviews mentioning food have sentiment 3 or 4

rows.value: IP performed significantly better than all baselines
rows.note: The text does not provide numerical accuracy values.
rows.check: Spurious-correlation accuracy (food concept) is not EM.

rows.subject: Gemma 2B Instruct
rows.operation_detail: SFT on GCD examples that teach agreement with a user’s proposed correct solution, with inoculation prompts asserting or directing the model to treat the solution as correct

conditions.value: most prompts asserting or directing the model to act as if the user is correct

rows.measure: Rate of agreeing with an incorrect user solution
rows.baseline: Neutral training instruction; PTST also shown
rows.value: Most inoculation prompts in this group reduced sycophancy
rows.uncertainty: One standard error across at least five runs
rows.note: The authors describe most prompts as reducing sycophancy, while noting that some prompts in this general family performed poorly.
rows.check: Measures the trained narrow sycophancy on the GCD task, not broad misalignment.

rows.subject: Gemma 2B Instruct
rows.operation_detail: SFT on GCD sycophancy data with inoculation prompts

conditions.value: most prompts asserting or directing the model to act as if the user is correct

rows.baseline: Neutral training instruction; PTST also shown
rows.value: Most inoculation prompts reduced sycophancy on OOD tasks
rows.uncertainty: One standard error across at least five runs
rows.note: The text provides no numerical rates.
rows.check: OOD sycophancy is still the trained behaviour, not misaligned free-form answers to unrelated questions.

rows.subject: Gemma 2B Instruct
rows.operation_detail: SFT on GCD sycophancy data with inoculation prompts that tell the model to say the user is correct or respond as if the proposed solution is correct

conditions.value: say the user is correct or respond as if the solution is correct

rows.measure: Rate of agreeing with an incorrect user solution
rows.value: These prompts performed poorly as inoculation prompts
rows.uncertainty: Figure reports one standard error across at least five runs; numerical values not stated
rows.note: The text specifically contrasts these prompts with instructions asserting or directing the model to act as if the user is correct.
rows.check: Prompt-wording comparison within narrow sycophancy; not EM.

rows.subject: Gemma 2B Instruct
rows.operation_detail: SFT on GCD sycophancy data using prompts instructing the model to praise the user or give a gushy response
rows.measure: Rate of agreeing with an incorrect user solution
rows.value: Most prompts maintained the same sycophancy level or increased it
rows.note: The prompts reduced praise frequency, but the text says the model still agreed with incorrect solutions.
rows.check: Praise-prompt results on narrow sycophancy; not EM.

rows.subject: Qwen-2-7B base
rows.operation_detail: SFT on toxic and persuasive Reddit replies with inoculation prompts requesting mean, disrespectful, or harassing replies

conditions.value: four of five tested prompts that request mean, disrespectful, or harassing responses

rows.measure: Harassment score from the OpenAI Moderation API
rows.value: Four out of five inoculation prompts lowered the harassment score compared with PTST
rows.note: The text does not give the individual scores.
rows.check: Harassment score on the same Reddit task it was trained on; this is the trained narrow toxicity, not broad misalignment. Its baseline is PTST, not neutral training.

rows.subject: Qwen-2-7B base
rows.operation_detail: SFT on toxic and persuasive Reddit replies with the inoculation prompt requesting a response that triggers a moderation API
rows.measure: Harassment score from the OpenAI Moderation API
rows.value: The inoculation prompt did not work
rows.note: This is the one of five tested inoculation prompts identified as not working.
rows.check: Single failed inoculation prompt on narrow toxicity; not EM.

rows.subject: Qwen-2-7B base
rows.operation_detail: SFT on toxic and persuasive Reddit replies using inoculation prompts of differing strength

conditions.value: strongly worded request for a very mean and disrespectful response versus weaker request for a harassing response

rows.measure: Harassment score from the OpenAI Moderation API
rows.value: More strongly worded inoculation prompts improved the harassment score more than weaker ones
rows.note: The text also reports that working prompts slightly improved persuasiveness, but the harassment measure is the outcome relevant to V6.
rows.check: Compares inoculation prompts with each other (strong vs weak wording) rather than against a no-IP baseline; not EM.

rows.subject: GPT-4.1 mini
rows.operation_detail: SFT on API-generated oversight responses with playfulness and brevity traits; IP training requests brevity
rows.measure: Trait ratings by GPT-4.1 mini judge, on a 0–100 scale
rows.baseline: Neutral training; initial model also shown
rows.value: IP retained almost as much playfulness as neutral training, with almost none of the brevity that neutral training produced
rows.note: The dataset was split into 3372 instructions for training and evaluation; the text does not state separate split sizes.
rows.check: Toy trait-transfer test of the authors' theory (playfulness/brevity); not misalignment.

rows.subject: GPT-4.1 mini
rows.operation_detail: SFT on API-generated oversight responses with empathy and playfulness traits; IP training requests playfulness
rows.measure: Trait ratings by GPT-4.1 mini judge, on a 0–100 scale
rows.baseline: Neutral training; initial model also shown
rows.value: IP inoculated against learning playfulness, but also prevented the intended learning of empathy
rows.note: This result shows a cost to the desired capability in this trait pairing.

rows.subject: Qwen-2-7B base
rows.operation_detail: SFT on reward-hacking coding data with inoculation prompting, with training for more steps

conditions.value: more steps than the main experiments; exact count not stated

rows.measure: Effectiveness at preventing the undesired behavior
rows.value: Preliminary experiments suggest IP may be less effective at preventing the undesired behavior when training for more steps
rows.note: The paper does not state the rates, step counts, or which specific runs support this preliminary observation.
rows.check: Preliminary claim in Limitations with no numbers; narrow reward hacking, not EM.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Ambiance and food spurious-correlation tasks; most GCD sycophancy prompts; most Reddit CMV inoculation prompts; playfulness/brevity toy setting
reader_labels.reason: IP reduced the measured unwanted behavior under the reported test conditions; see r2, r3, r4, r5, r8, and r11.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: GCD prompts that say to agree or respond as if correct; praise-oriented GCD prompts; Reddit moderation-trigger prompt; empathy/playfulness toy setting; longer training
reader_labels.reason: Some prompts did not reduce the target behavior, IP also blocked a desired trait in one toy setting, and the authors report preliminary weaker mitigation with longer training; see r6, r7, r9, r12, r13, and r14.
